items.summary: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war. Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days. But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal. "They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously. "They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

items.title: US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis
items.summary: US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis The Justice Department has arrested a man under claims that he attempted to provide material support or resources to Yemen’s Houthis. The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. "As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives". "These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination," he added. Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear before a federal judge on 2 October in Washington.

items.title: Lessons from the Iran War
items.summary: The Iran war offers broader lessons about the limits of force, the resilience of revolutionary regimes, and the unpredictability of modern conflict. Military action can weaken an adversary without producing decisive political outcomes, while economic pressure, alliances, energy markets, and public opinion can prove equally consequential. The conflict also exposed vulnerabilities in alliance coordination, munitions stocks, counter-drone capabilities, and strategic communication. Effective deterrence ultimately requires hard power, resilient partnerships, clear objectives, and the political will to sustain them.

Trump added that the case "might be" linked to Iran but declined to give details. "I'm surprised that they released them; I wouldn't have done that," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, while adding that British authorities had worked "very closely" with the US. "We know everything about them. We would not have released them." The five men were arrested early on Sunday near the Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford base in southwest England, from which US bombers have taken off to target Iran since March.

items.title: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports
items.summary: Riyadh schools to operate remotely for week, AFP reports Parents across Riyadh received emails from schools on Sunday announcing a last-minute plan to shift to remote learning for a week, according to messages seen by AFP. "We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. There was no official reason given but the move comes amid heightened tensions in the Gulf and near-daily attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi fighters in Yemen. "When a decision affects an entire school community for a full week, families deserve clear communication and transparency about the reasons behind it," one parent living in Riyadh who spoke on condition of anonymity told AFP. "It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added. The announcement comes a day after the Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis said it had intercepted drones and ballistic missiles targeting the kingdom. The strikes were the latest in a series of escalating Houthi attacks

Airport director Hussein Muhanna told AFP that the flights have been halted between Najaf, a holy city south of Baghdad, following a directive from the prime minister's office to the governor. items.summary: UK warns Iran it will not tolerate hostile activity on its soil Britain's foreign minister met his Iranian counterpart on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York and told him his country would "not tolerate intimidation, threats or hostile activity on UK soil" from groups linked to Iran. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi also discussed the war in the Middle East and the importance of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. "The Foreign Secretary reiterated the UK's unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups on UK soil, including attacks on the British Jewish community," a Foreign Office statement said. A statement on Araghchi’s Telegram account said he had used the meeting to call for a correction to "the destructive and irresponsible approaches of some European governments towards Iran and regional developments." He also said an "insistence on interfering in countries’ internal affairs and the instrumental use of human rights concepts is in no way acceptable."

items.title: Saudi-led coalition claims Houthis targeted power station in Medina
items.summary: Saudi-led coalition claims Houthis targeted power station in Medina The Saudi-led pro-government coalition in Yemen has claimed that the Houthi rebel group targeted a power centre in Medina in a drone attack on Tuesday, damaging one transformer but leaving the overall electricity network unaffected. Medina, in Saudi Arabia's western Hejaz region, is among the holiest cities in Islam. The Houthis, officially called Ansar Allah, have seized territory in Yemen's southwest this month in a rapid offensive triggered by the Saudi bombing of Sanaa airport in July. The group has also bombed the Saudi East-West oil pipeline, through which Riyadh has diverted oil exports amid Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. But the Houthis previously denied Saudi claims that they had targeted Mecca, the holiest place in Islam.

Ook zijn volgens de Britse autoriteiten twee panden in hetzelfde gebied doorzocht. In het onderzoek is ook een 26-jarige Brit verhoord. Afgelopen zondag werden vijf Britse mannen, tussen de 23 en 25 jaar, aangehouden in de buurt van de basis van de Royal Air Force bij Fairford in het graafschap Gloucestershire. Ze worden verdacht van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag. Op de luchtmachtbasis zijn naast Britse militairen ook Amerikaanse militairen en bommenwerpers gestationeerd. Die vliegbasis wordt gebruikt in de oorlog tegen Iran. De antiterreurpolitie zegt alle mogelijke scenario's te onderzoeken, ook of sprake is van buitenlandse inmenging. items.title: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran
items.summary: Colombia's new US-backed government cuts ties with Iran Colombia said on Thursday it had cut diplomatic ties with Iran, the latest Washington ally in Latin America to sever links with the US arch-foe. Colombia's new right-wing president, Abelardo de la Espriella, has redrawn Colombia's alliances since taking over from his leftist predecessor Gustavo Petro on 7 August with the full-throated endorsement of US President Donald Trump. De la Espriella's government accused the Iranian government of having ties to "narco-terrorist groups that threaten the security of the country," without giving proof of the allegations. Iran's foreign ministry hit back on Friday, calling the allegations "baseless claims". "It is clear that none of the claims put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this decision has been made solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States."

items.title: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran
items.summary: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran Colombia on Thursday announced that it formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing it "deteriorated" in Tehran. The Foreign Ministry said the decision took effect on Saturday due to "national and hemispheric security concerns," accusing Iran of human rights violations as well as alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups. "Colombia also took into account confirmed human rights violations, verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities' obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran's nuclear program," the ministry said. "These facts deteriorated Colombia’s trust in the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

items.summary: Houthi advance on Aden supply route repelled, say Saudi-backed forces Yemen's Saudi-backed forces said on Thursday that they had repelled overnight attacks by the Houthis on a key supply route to the southern port city of Aden, where the government is based. The mountain pass known as Hejat al-Abd is a lifeline for forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which has been hemmed in by a lightning Houthi advance this month linked to the war on Iran. The road is also critical for goods entering Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, and its southern and western rural areas, Reuters reported. It is the only route for residents seeking to travel abroad, with no commercial flights operating from Houthi-controlled areas. The Iran-aligned Houthis have kept up pressure on government forces as they seek to consolidate gains made nearly two weeks ago, when their offensive along Yemen's western coast brought them to the shores of the Red Sea's strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, through which at least ten percent of global maritime trade usually passes.

items.summary: Since the U.S. war against Iran started earlier this year, Washington has pressed its allies in Europe and Asia to “ step up ” with military aid to help the United States reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Despite persistent pressure from both Trump administration officials and President Donald Trump himself , most U.S. allies have remained reluctant . Those who have chosen to provide support have done so largely in an indirect capacity, such as by permitting limited base access. South Korea has been a major target of that pressure. In August, Trump abruptly announced on social media that Washington will “substantially reduce” U.S.-South Korea joint military exercises, linking the decision to Seoul’s continued refusal to support his war efforts against Iran. Trump’s apparent retaliation alarmed Seoul and sparked a serious debate over whether to deploy its navy to the Strait of Hormuz. Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. Volodymyr Zelenskyy delivered an account of five years of Russian aggression: the staggering loss of life – hundreds of thousands killed on both sides – the porousness of the sanctions on Russia, the “madness” of it all. items.summary: Ethiopia is on the brink of another civil war. Last week, fighting between rebels and federal forces in the northern Tigray, Amhara, and Afar states left hundreds dead. items.summary: Vance describes Iran’s leadership as ‘very confused’, says deal possible US Vice President JD Vance said there is still scope for a deal with Iran if its leaders honour their commitments to Washington, while describing Tehran’s political decision-making system as “very confused”. In an interview with journalist Vince Coglianese, Vance said President Donald Trump had made clear that “there is a universe where we can strike a deal with Iran, but that requires the Iranians to behave”. He said Washington’s approach would be based on Iranian actions rather than statements. Vance said Iran’s leadership involved “a number of different constituencies”, including hardliners, conservatives, moderates and clerics. He also said Iran’s new supreme leader was “very detached” and not involved in day-to-day decision-making or public discussions about negotiations.

items.summary: By any measure, 2026 has been a disastrous year for President Donald Trump’s foreign policy. An Iran war in which Trump promised quick victory has turned into a protracted farce dragging down the world economy. The president’s “reciprocal tariffs” were gutted by the Supreme Court, and his administration’s trade agenda remains deeply unpopular . Even his regime change operation in Venezuela, an apparent success, was broadly rejected by the American public and has put the United States into an imperial caretaker role in that country that could prove complicated and costly. It is no surprise, then, that the president’s approval rating on foreign policy has sunk by almost 30% since his inauguration for his second term. With Trump’s overall polling numbers cratering, Democrats appear to have a decisive advantage in November’s midterms. items.summary: There’s something profoundly human about the scapegoat. From the ancient Israelites and Greeks to the Aztecs , global cultures have long sought to concentrate society’s ills in a single vessel, cleansing the rest of us in the process. Today, the Democratic foreign-policy establishment is looking for a scapegoat of its own. Tainted by the sins of enabling Israeli conduct in Gaza and beyond, many national-security mandarins are seeking absolution by proxy, perhaps in hopes of returning to the halls of power in 2029. Joe Biden has emerged as the bearer of these iniquities. As numerous former Biden administration officials have asked me over the past year, can you really blame the bureaucrats for implementing the whims of an obstinate president? In his new book, “Crossing the Red Line,” journalist Akbar Shahid Ahmed offers the first comprehensive opportunity to evaluate this scapegoating exercise. First, the inflationary risks of throwing subsidies at the housing market at a moment when wider inflation, driven by energy prices and the Iran war, is on the march. Second, the political awkwardness of turning to George Osborne’s playbook. Third, the spectre of Jeff Fairburn, the shameless former boss of Persimmon who bagged a £75m bonus in 2018 as help to buy turbo-charged the value of his share-based incentives. Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the start of the war in late February, made the remarks despite attempts to revive talks aimed at ending the fighting. "Today, having suffered painful blows at the hands of valiant fighters and the guardians of the Strait of Hormuz, they (the enemies) do not venture beyond the Arabian Sea," Khamenei said in the written statement attributed to him, without explicitly mentioning the United States. "Whenever they have braved this risk, they have only brought harm upon themselves. It will not be long before the Arabian Sea, too, would rid itself of their presence," he added.

clusters.headline: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention

items.title: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention
items.summary: Palestinian-American journalist freed after 13 days in Israeli detention Palestinian-American journalist Naqaa Hamed was released from Damon Prison after 13 days, following an Israeli court decision. Hamed was arrested on 15 September at the Tuqu checkpoint while returning from an assignment, was separated from her camera crew and taken to an unknown location for questioning. Hamed was arrested on suspicion of “cooperating with an enemy entity” and possible espionage, according to Israeli media at the time. She previously served as a correspondent for Iran’s Press TV in the occupied West Bank. According to the Palestinian Prisoners’ Society, 36 Palestinian journalists, including four women, remain detained in Israeli jails, along with about 90 Palestinian women.

clusters.headline: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

items.title: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?
items.summary: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues? For more than two decades, Iraq 's oil wealth has passed through a financial system centred thousands of miles away in New York. The arrangement, created after the US -led invasion of Iraq in 2003, was initially designed to protect Iraqi oil revenues from creditors and help fund reconstruction. Today, it gives Washington significant leverage over Iraq's access to its own dollars, leverage that the US is increasingly using as it pressures Baghdad to curb Iran 's influence and the activities of armed groups aligned with Tehran. The issue came into sharp focus in April, when Washington blocked a shipment of about $500m in cash to Iraq as it pressured the government over Iran-aligned armed groups. Muayen al-Kadhimi, a former parliamentary Finance Committee member, condemned the decision at the time, calling on the government to end what he described as US dominance over Iraqi funds. Read more: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

Israel, which has occupied dozens of villages south of the Litani River since its latest invasion of the country earlier this year can't wait for the Blue Helmets to leave. It has long lobbied against UNIFIL’s extension, deeming it ineffective in taming and disarming Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia. But Tel Aviv hasn't opposed an international force once UNIFIL leaves; it just doesn’t want one tied to the UN. His comments come as Tehran continues to assess the impact of the war and reinforce its military infrastructure.

Minister Araghchi is in New York voor de Algemene Vergadering van de Verenigde Naties. Daar zei hij tegen verslaggevers dat dit mogelijk is als "aan de noodzakelijke voorwaarden wordt voldaan". Die voorwaarden komen uit een eerdere overeenkomst tussen de VS en Iran die in juni werd ondertekend en waarmee een staakt-het-vuren werd verlengd, dat daarna volop werd geschonden . In die overeenkomst stond dat de VS en Iran alle militaire operaties zouden staken en dat het stoppen met militaire acties ook gold voor Libanon waar Israël aanvallen uitvoert. Ook zou de VS de zeeblokkade opheffen en Iran zou een veilige doorgang bieden voor commerciële schepen. Daarnaast was afgesproken dat Iran geen kernwapens zou ontwikkelen of aanschaffen. items.summary: EU warns of energy 'price crisis', asks countries to consider curbing demand The European Union is facing an energy price crisis as a result of the Iran war fallout in oil and gas markets, the bloc's energy chief said on Friday in a letter seen by Reuters, which urged countries to consider measures to curb energy demand. "We are facing a price crisis linking to a supply crisis," EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen said in a letter to EU countries' energy ministers. While the EU is better prepared now than it was in winter 2021 when Russia squeezed Europe's gas supplies by reducing deliveries, governments must step up preparations for this winter, he said. "I invite you to consider taking or continuing to take measures that can sustain [gas storage] injections or reduce gas and electricity demand for as long as necessary," Jorgensen said.

items.summary: When the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran ultimately ends, it will be remembered for its bloody onset. On the same day airstrikes killed the Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, a U.S. missile incinerated an elementary school in Minab, killing 123 children and dozens of others. Some 250 miles away, U.S. missiles fell on a residential area of Lamerd, killing 21 civilians, including five children. Neither the White House nor Pentagon has publicly admitted responsibility in either incident, although an internal review reportedly determined Minab was hit by a U.S. missile. clusters.headline: The west is in freefall – and the worst part is that we were warned, but chose not to listen | Owen Jones

items.title: The west is in freefall – and the worst part is that we were warned, but chose not to listen | Owen Jones
items.summary: Endless pursuit of wealth and power by western leaders led us here. What strikes me most is how many saw what was coming The symptoms of decline are everywhere you look. On Sunday, Germany’s far right won another state election , taking nearly 40% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. France is preparing a €54bn fiscal squeeze, which could turn the screw still further on a foundering so-called European social model. At the UN general assembly, Donald Trump once again threatened to “annihilate” Iran, even as the fourth failed western war on a Muslim nation this century has added more than $100bn to Americans’ fuel bills. items.summary: US prosecutors probing Binance for possible Iran sanctions violations US prosecutors are investigating Binance in connection to US sanctions on Iran and trading activity on its platform, a source with knowledge of the matter said. The investigation is being led by federal prosecutors with the US attorney's office in Manhattan and with the Justice Department's criminal division in Washington, the source said. Bloomberg News, which earlier reported the probe, said investigators are scrutinising whether Binance knowingly allowed the trading that violated the sanctions. Spokespeople for the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York and the Justice Department's criminal division declined to comment. Binance said in a statement it has a zero-tolerance approach to sanctions violations. "We fully cooperate with law enforcement, and we remain committed to rooting out and shutting down bad actors," it said. items.summary: Aan de opmars van de Houthi's in Jemen lijkt voorlopig geen einde te komen. Als dat lukt, wordt de greep van de Houthi's op de Straat van Bab al-Mandab nog steviger. En dat terwijl de Houthi's een maand geleden alleen nog het noordwesten van Jemen onder controle hadden. Sinds juli is het geweld tussen de militante groepering en Saudi-Arabië opgelaaid, en onlangs begonnen de Houthi's een grondoffensief. Daarbij namen ze al de steden Mokka en Dhubab en het eiland Perim in, waarmee het de controle over de belangrijke zeestraat Bab al-Mandab in handen kreeg. Die is belangrijk voor de internationale zeevaart, zeker nu de Straat van Hormuz sinds februari vrijwel afgesloten is vanwege de oorlog tussen de VS en Iran. Daarmee hebben de Houthi's een belangrijke troef in handen. Toch ondervonden ze weinig weerstand bij hun opmars naar de zeestraat. Hoe konden de Houthi's zo snel en ogenschijnlijk makkelijk oprukken? In augustus ging het nog om een stijging van 3,3 procent ten opzichte van een jaar eerder. Naast motorbrandstoffen is volgens hoofdeconoom Peter Hein van Mulligen steeds meer te zien dat ook andere energie zoals elektriciteit duurder wordt. "In de eerste helft van het jaar was het telkens goedkoper dan een jaar eerder. Nu is dat niet meer zo." Boodschappen zijn voor de tweede maand op rij iets goedkoper geworden, maar als de energieprijzen hoog blijven is het volgens Van Mulligen de vraag hoelang dat zal duren. Op wat langere termijn leiden hogere energieprijzen ook weer tot hogere prijzen in de winkel, omdat productiekosten oplopen. "Hoelang dat duurt is altijd een beetje afwachten", zegt Van Mulligen. "Doorgaans duurt het ongeveer een half jaar. Het kan iets korter of langer zijn." Extreme effecten zoals in 2022 verwacht Van Mulligen niet. "De inflatie ligt nu een stuk lager." items.title: Red scare: Solid GOP districts reeling from war, price backlash
items.summary: On Monday, as the war with Iran crossed the seven-month mark, Governor Greg Abbott declared a statewide disaster in Texas as a result of a massive increase in diesel prices and a deepening fuel shortage. Texas is hardly alone. Diesel prices have climbed nationwide since the war began, with the national average now around $6.45 per gallon , up from $3.76 when the war began in late February, according to data from AAA. A number of other states have recently taken steps to try to ease the costs of gas and diesel amid the ongoing war. As the midterm elections near and the war’s costs hit voters’ wallets, Abbott's declaration is a window into a larger problem for Republicans across the country, including some in deep red states. An increasing number of Republicans are being forced to spend money and political capital defending seats that they carried easily in recent elections. “The Iran War is proving to be a drag on Republicans, even in solidly Republican states,” Brian Darling, a Republican strategist and former counsel to Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.), told Responsible Statecraft in an email

The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. "As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives". items.title: War, power games and impunity. I watched the farce that is the UN general assembly: what a tragedy, what a mess | Nesrine Malik

Seen up close, it is a study in stasis and decline UN general assembly meetings are not usually riveting occasions. But this year’s encapsulated a world in flux and crisis, an international law and organisation structure that is falling apart, and a humanitarian order machine running hot. What unfolded was less a gathering for resolution and resolve than a display of showboating, frustration and fractiousness. It was a snapshot for the history books of four huge destabilising conflicts for which there seems to be no means of, or interest in, resolution – Ukraine, Iran, Palestine and Sudan. Volodymyr Zelenskyy delivered an account of five years of Russian aggression: the staggering loss of life – hundreds of thousands killed on both sides – the porousness of the sanctions on Russia, the “madness” of it all. Hegseth praised the American troops he addressed, crediting them with having destroyed Iran’s “entire defense space”. “Iran’s conventional shield has been crippled, and their nuclear ambitions have been crippled and laid bare for the world,” he added. Hegseth said the Pentagon has undergone a “clear break” from its past, with a “singular mission” of war-fighting. He said the department had fired “nearly 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force”, a figure he framed as “accountability” rather than a “purge”, as some media have called it. items.title: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase scare
items.summary: UK PM says 'strong indications' Iran involved in airbase scare British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday there were "strong indications" that Iran was involved in suspicious activity at a UK airbase that triggered a major security incident. "There are strong indications that Iran played a part in what happened over the weekend at RAF Fairford," Burnham told the BBC in an interview, referring to suspected bomb threat near the airbase in southwest England, which is used by the US military in its campaign against Tehran. Iran has denied involvement in the incident, and the five men arrested on suspicion of terrorist offences were later released on bail, with counterterrorism police saying that no improvised explosive devices were found in their vehicle, but a quantity of petrol was discovered.

items.title: Goodnight Baghdad: US troops leave Iraq after 23 years
items.summary: The Iraq War was already four-years-old when I walked down the ramp of a C-17 at Al Taqaddum Air Base in April 2007. The fact that I am writing these words is proof that I survived that deployment and a subsequent one to Afghanistan in 2013. In the years since, I transitioned back into civilian life, established a new career, and saw my kids grow up and escape the nest. During nearly all of that time, there were still American troops on the ground in Iraq. I have a son serving in the military today. He has never been to Iraq, but I can absolutely sympathize with the Iraq veterans who came home from the war only to see their sons or daughters deploy to the same war zone. items.title: Venezuela blowback may have a long fuse. It always does.
items.summary: In 1927, Augusto Cesar Sandino began an insurgent campaign against the U.S. occupation of Nicaragua. Under orders from President Calvin Coolidge, the U.S. Marines had intervened in Nicaragua to settle a civil war between a conservative government and liberal rebels. In his manifesto , Sandino responded by effectively declaring war on the United States. He also specifically denounced former liberal leaders who had agreed to put down their arms in the face of U.S. intervention. Speaking of General Moncada, the leading liberal officer who had agreed to end his revolt in talks convened by future Secretary of State Henry Stimson, Sandino wrote: “Nobody gave him the authority to abandon the ranks of the revolution to make secret agreements with the enemy.” One imagines there are Chavistas in Venezuela with similar feelings about interim President Delcy Rodriguez right now. Having intervened to end the civil war in Nicaragua, the U.S. soon found itself embroiled in a bitter counter-insurgency campaign against Sandino’s men. items.title: Ex-Biden officials are desperate for a Gaza scapegoat
items.summary: There’s something profoundly human about the scapegoat. From the ancient Israelites and Greeks to the Aztecs , global cultures have long sought to concentrate society’s ills in a single vessel, cleansing the rest of us in the process. Today, the Democratic foreign-policy establishment is looking for a scapegoat of its own. Tainted by the sins of enabling Israeli conduct in Gaza and beyond, many national-security mandarins are seeking absolution by proxy, perhaps in hopes of returning to the halls of power in 2029. items.title: Lessons from the Iran War
items.summary: The Iran war offers broader lessons about the limits of force, the resilience of revolutionary regimes, and the unpredictability of modern conflict. Military action can weaken an adversary without producing decisive political outcomes, while economic pressure, alliances, energy markets, and public opinion can prove equally consequential. The conflict also exposed vulnerabilities in alliance coordination, munitions stocks, counter-drone capabilities, and strategic communication. Effective deterrence ultimately requires hard power, resilient partnerships, clear objectives, and the political will to sustain them.

items.title: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?
items.summary: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues? For more than two decades, Iraq 's oil wealth has passed through a financial system centred thousands of miles away in New York. The arrangement, created after the US -led invasion of Iraq in 2003, was initially designed to protect Iraqi oil revenues from creditors and help fund reconstruction. Today, it gives Washington significant leverage over Iraq's access to its own dollars, leverage that the US is increasingly using as it pressures Baghdad to curb Iran 's influence and the activities of armed groups aligned with Tehran. The issue came into sharp focus in April, when Washington blocked a shipment of about $500m in cash to Iraq as it pressured the government over Iran-aligned armed groups. Muayen al-Kadhimi, a former parliamentary Finance Committee member, condemned the decision at the time, calling on the government to end what he described as US dominance over Iraqi funds. Read more: Why does the US control Iraq's oil revenues?

Zowel bij bemande als onbemande tankstations daar steeg het aantal Nederlandse pinbetalingen hard, met 20 procent. Daarop sloot Iran de Straat van Hormuz af. Sindsdien staat de olie-export onder druk . Psychologische grens Het ligt voor de hand dat prijsverschillen een rol speelden, zegt DNB. items.title: Ben-Gvir nella cella del comandante di Hamas: “Ti farò giustiziare, per te sarà l'inferno”
items.summary: Il ministro israeliano della Sicurezza nazionale Itamar Ben-Gvir ha diffuso un video in cui affronta in carcere Hassan Salama, alto esponente delle Brigate al-Qassam di Hamas: «Voglio ucciderti, ti farò giustiziare». Ben-Gvir indossa una spilla a forma di cappio e dice al detenuto che per lui «sarà l’inferno». Salama sta scontando 48 ergastoli dopo essere stato condannato per aver organizzato una serie di attentati suicidi del 1996 che uccisero decine di israeliani e ne ferirono centinaia. Data e luogo delle riprese non sono stati verificati in modo indipendente. A marzo la Knesset ha approvato una legge che introduce la pena di morte in specifici casi di terrorismo, sostenuta da Ben-Gvir. items.title: Israel wants US-led force to disarm Lebanon's Hezbollah
items.summary: Fearing a security vacuum if UN peacekeepers leave southern Lebanon when their mandate expires December 31, the Lebanese government is desperately seeking an extension of the United Nations Interim Force (UNIFIL) or the creation of a European-led multinational force to take its place. Israel, which has occupied dozens of villages south of the Litani River since its latest invasion of the country earlier this year can't wait for the Blue Helmets to leave. It has long lobbied against UNIFIL’s extension, deeming it ineffective in taming and disarming Hezbollah, the Iran-backed militia. But Tel Aviv hasn't opposed an international force once UNIFIL leaves; it just doesn’t want one tied to the UN. Israel is lobbying for a U.S.-led force, while the Lebanese government prefers a European-led mission to aid the Lebanese army if UNIFIL’s mandate is not renewed or extended. An even bigger question is how exactly any such force can subdue battle-hardened Hezbollah, the country’s most powerful armed force. Hasta que Donald Trump y Benjamin Netanyahu decidieron lanzar su guerra sorpresa contra Teherán el 28 de febrero , la respuesta era clara: el líder supremo, Alí Jamenei. Ese mismo día, Estados Unidos e Israel asesinaron a Jamenei, máxima autoridad desde que tomó el relevo de Ruhola Jomeini en 1989.Las autoridades islámicas tardaron un mes en llenar ese vacío de poder y designaron a Mojtaba , su hijo, como nuevo guía del país. "We have just been informed by Saudi authorities that schools must remain closed all week," read two separate messages seen by AFP. "It's a last-minute decision. We have no clue what's happening," a Lebanese expatriate living in Riyadh added. He also supported initiatives aimed at de-escalation, particularly efforts by Qatar and Pakistan, saying they can help restore regional stability. The minister accused Iran of flagrant attacks on civilian and economic targets across the region, while calling on the international community to condemn Houthi actions threatening Red Sea shipping.

items.title: At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping
items.summary: At UN, Saudi FM warns world failing to protect Gulf shipping Saudi Arabia warned UN members Saturday that attempts to block Middle East waterways are a threat to global energy security and demanded the international community do more to defend freedom of navigation. Since the United States and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, Tehran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while its Houthi allies in Yemen have subsequently done the same in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. Both waterways are vital routes for oil and gas exports. "The international community has been absent from assuming its responsibilities in confronting all that threatens international peace and security," Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan told the United Nations General Assembly. "The kingdom stresses the importance of guaranteeing the protection of freedom of navigation in all international waterways, foremost among them the Strait of Hormuz, the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden," he said.

items.summary: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Hormuz and end war US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Iran war. Iran raised the initiative at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators and that it could reopen the strategic waterway and put an end to hostilities in the region within seven days. But in comments to reporters at the White House, Trump said: "I reject their proposal. ... I rejected their deal. "They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," he said before leaving for Tennessee. "We're winning tremendously. "They want to make a deal and I think that's fine, I like making a deal too. What they want to do is immediately open the Hormuz Strait ... because they have no money coming in, because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait," Trump said.

Iran moves key defence capabilities underground, Tasnim reports
items.summary: Iran moves key defence capabilities underground, Tasnim reports Iran has relocated part of its army’s strategic capabilities to underground facilities to prevent adversaries from gaining a complete understanding of its defence capabilities and weapons production capacity, the country's defence ministry spokesman, Reza Talaei-Nik, has said, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Talaei-Nik said the United States had failed to achieve its strategic objectives in the war on Iran, including efforts to weaken Iran’s strategic position in the region. He said Iran had instead “imposed costs on the enemy”, according to Tasnim. The defence ministry spokesman also said Iran needed to simultaneously strengthen its defence capabilities and domestic capacity. His comments come as Tehran continues to assess the impact of the war and reinforce its military infrastructure.

items.title: The truth behind Donald Trump’s ‘biggest oil deal in world history’
items.summary: The US’s oil deal with Venezuela faces multiple legal and logistical problems, including questions about whether it can be implemented Donald Trump has long coveted the oilfields of other nations and declared an agreement with Venezuela to be “the biggest oil deal in world history”. But the agreement, reached after the US seized Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro, is almost certainly doomed to collapse amid a wide array of legal and logistical issues, a Guardian investigation has found. The US president first mused about taking oil from Iran in 1987, when he told ABC’s Barbara Walters that Iranian attacks on American shipping during the Iran-Iraq war required an extreme response. “Why couldn’t we go in and take over some of their oil, which is along the sea?” he asked. items.title: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days
items.summary: Iran proposes plan to reopen Hormuz within seven days Araghchi met for talks on Tuesday with US President Donald Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff, and previously set out conditions for ending the war and reopening the vital energy shipping channel. "Iran has conveyed to the United States, through Qatar, a concrete seven-day plan. If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, and normal maritime passage restored within seven days," Araghchi said at the UN Friday. "The choice now rests with the United States. Iran does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation, and Iran will not surrender its sovereign rights under pressure. "I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared." Earlier media reports suggest the new plan calls for a seven-day cessation of all hostilities in the Middle East, including in Lebanon.

"We are facing a price crisis linking to a supply crisis," EU energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen said in a letter to EU countries' energy ministers. While the EU is better prepared now than it was in winter 2021 when Russia squeezed Europe's gas supplies by reducing deliveries, governments must step up preparations for this winter, he said. "I invite you to consider taking or continuing to take measures that can sustain [gas storage] injections or reduce gas and electricity demand for as long as necessary," Jorgensen said.

"The Foreign Secretary reiterated the UK's unwavering resolve to combat threats from Iranian-linked groups on UK soil, including attacks on the British Jewish community," a Foreign Office statement said. items.title: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran
items.summary: Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran Colombia on Thursday announced that it formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing it "deteriorated" in Tehran. The Foreign Ministry said the decision took effect on Saturday due to "national and hemispheric security concerns," accusing Iran of human rights violations as well as alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups. "Colombia also took into account confirmed human rights violations, verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities' obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency's (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran's nuclear program," the ministry said. "These facts deteriorated Colombia’s trust in the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran."

items.summary: Since the U.S. war against Iran started earlier this year, Washington has pressed its allies in Europe and Asia to “ step up ” with military aid to help the United States reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Despite persistent pressure from both Trump administration officials and President Donald Trump himself , most U.S. allies have remained reluctant . Those who have chosen to provide support have done so largely in an indirect capacity, such as by permitting limited base access. South Korea has been a major target of that pressure. Trump’s apparent retaliation alarmed Seoul and sparked a serious debate over whether to deploy its navy to the Strait of Hormuz. On the same day airstrikes killed the Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, a U.S. missile incinerated an elementary school in Minab, killing 123 children and dozens of others. Some 250 miles away, U.S. missiles fell on a residential area of Lamerd, killing 21 civilians, including five children. Neither the White House nor Pentagon has publicly admitted responsibility in either incident, although an internal review reportedly determined Minab was hit by a U.S. missile. items.title: Iranian elite profiting from oil sanctions
items.summary: Iranian elite profiting from oil sanctions International sanctions against Iran have created lucrative financial channels, generating substantial profits for people linked to the country's security institutions, local media has reported. Yashar Soltani, an Iranian investigative journalist, alleged that the Ministry of Petroleum has lost control of marketing and exporting the country's national oil industry, handing it to an exclusive network of four brokers who circumvent international sanctions. Soltani, who has previously been jailed for reporting on financial corruption, said brokers have a strong financial incentive to disrupt political agreements between Tehran and Washington, as lifting sanctions would effectively shut down the networks through which they operate. According to Soltani, Mohammad Javad Bavand, a former economic deputy at the intelligence organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, is overseeing the sale of Iranian oil and has, over the past three months, granted four brokers rights to sell 80m barrels of oil. items.title: Houthi advance on Aden supply route repelled, say Saudi-backed forces
items.summary: Houthi advance on Aden supply route repelled, say Saudi-backed forces Yemen's Saudi-backed forces said on Thursday that they had repelled overnight attacks by the Houthis on a key supply route to the southern port city of Aden, where the government is based. The mountain pass known as Hejat al-Abd is a lifeline for forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's Saudi-backed government, which has been hemmed in by a lightning Houthi advance this month linked to the war on Iran. The road is also critical for goods entering Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, and its southern and western rural areas, Reuters reported. It is the only route for residents seeking to travel abroad, with no commercial flights operating from Houthi-controlled areas. The Iran-aligned Houthis have kept up pressure on government forces as they seek to consolidate gains made nearly two weeks ago, when their offensive along Yemen's western coast brought them to the shores of the Red Sea's strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, through which at least ten percent of global maritime trade usually passes.

items.summary: Endless pursuit of wealth and power by western leaders led us here. What strikes me most is how many saw what was coming The symptoms of decline are everywhere you look. On Sunday, Germany’s far right won another state election , taking nearly 40% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. France is preparing a €54bn fiscal squeeze, which could turn the screw still further on a foundering so-called European social model. At the UN general assembly, Donald Trump once again threatened to “annihilate” Iran, even as the fourth failed western war on a Muslim nation this century has added more than $100bn to Americans’ fuel bills. There is little dispute over the symptoms. The great fight of our age is over the diagnosis, and the right has been winning it for years. Its story is simple and, as the latest German state election underlines, effective: the west is dying because of migrants, Muslims, trans people, “woke” and the “deep state”. items.summary: This article is co-published in partnership with The Intercept For the first time, the Pentagon budget topped $1 trillion and private contractors now receive more than half of all the tax dollars flowing to the Pentagon. Few have profited from this privatization of the U.S. military more than the CEOs of Pentagon contractors. While these companies often advertise their work as supporting the troops, the fact is that many servicemembers live in appalling housing conditions, while military-industrial contractors’ profits soar and their CEOs live in luxury. items.title: The Guardian view on the future of the UN: more embattled, but more necessary, than ever | Editorial
items.summary: As the secretary general, António Guterres, prepares to step down, the general assembly is highlighting the scale of the organisation’s challenges The United Nations was created, its charter states , to “save succeeding generations from the scourge of war”. Donald Trump used his address to the general assembly to threaten Iran , another member state, with annihilation again. The charter also speaks of the obligations of international law. On Venezuela, Mr Trump gloated that “to the victor belong the spoils”. His speech in New York on Tuesday might be regarded as an improvement on last year’s only in that it was not an explicit, full-scale attack on the UN itself, merely on its founding principles. The absences this year are perhaps as telling as the US president’s hostile presence. Vladimir Putin has not attended for more than a decade. Nor has Xi Jinping – but the snub is more striking as he is in Washington to meet the US president. items.title: Yemen crisis reminds Saudi Arabia of imperative to navigate tough realities
items.summary: For years, Saudi Arabia's security posture rested on a quiet assumption: that Washington would show up when it mattered. The dramatic events in Sept. 2019 tested that assumption directly. Claimed by Yemen’s Ansarullah movement but blamed on Iran, drone and missile strikes on the Abqaiq and Khurais oil facilities knocked out roughly half of Saudi production overnight—one of the most consequential attacks on Gulf Arab energy infrastructure in decades. The United States did not respond militarily. That non-response is now widely read as the moment the assumption broke.
